method: Each section read in full by a machine-assisted reviewer against the packs and the ground catalogue as of this date; not a legal review.

sections.bearsOn: Background only; states the objectives came from LRMPs and Crown land plans.
Whether a block lies in a mapped ADA or SRA decides whether the order's harvest pathways and conditions apply to it.
sections.gapNote: The ground screen reads the extent polygons from DataBC; every rule takes "does the order apply" as the reviewer's answer. The maps are marked DRAFT and not for legal purposes, so the screen can only suggest; a rule could pre-fill the applicability question from the screen as a candidate.
proposedFacts: Does the block or its road overlap an ADA or SRA polygon of the 2006 Omineca order as mapped by DataBC?
Has the district confirmed the block is inside the order's legal ADA or SRA boundary?

sections.bearsOn: Timber in an ADA or SRA is to be managed subject to Parts A to E, which the packs read as the only pathways to harvest there.
sections.gapNote: ada-sra-no-pathway reads Parts A, B and E as exhaustive. The text does not prohibit other harvest in words; that reading follows from "timber is to be managed subject to", and the finding should say it is the reading taken.

sections.bearsOn: A block in an ADA/SRA may be harvested for environmental or safety reasons only when proposed by local or provincial government, agreed by both ministries and directed by an operational work plan.

A forest-health block is allowed only for activities under the Bark Beetle Regulation or other forest health legislation, with a clear indication that the sanitation harvest will significantly assist in stopping spread to adjacent stands, and under Part C.
sections.gapNote: The rule tests the "clear indication" limb; nothing asks under which forest health enactment the harvest is carried out (the FPC Bark Beetle Regulation has since been repealed, so the reviewer should name the current authority).

sections.bearsOn: Conditions C.1 to C.6 apply only to forest practices permitted under Part B.
sections.gapNote: The packs scope Part C to Part B harvests, as the text says.

sections.bearsOn: A Part B block removes dead or infested timber only, taking live trees only for access, skidding or safety.
Stumps in a Part B block must be at least 15 cm high, lower only for access, skidding, landings or safety.
sections.gapNote: ada-sra-part-c fires on every Part B harvest and lists the condition as an action, but asks nothing; whether the site plan or cutting permit carries the 15 cm minimum is never tested.
proposedFacts: Does the site plan or cutting permit require stumps of at least 15 cm, except for access, skidding, landings or safety?

sections.bearsOn: Logging waste in a Part B block must be piled and burned or removed, not spread across the block.
sections.gapNote: Listed as an action only; no question asks how residue is to be treated.
proposedFacts: Is logging waste and residue to be piled and burned or removed rather than spread across the cutblock?

sections.bearsOn: Permanent roads (and gravelling) for a Part B block are to be minimized and placed along lot lines and natural boundaries as much as possible.
sections.gapNote: Listed as an action only. The road designer could measure permanent road length in the ADA/SRA and its distance from cadastral lot lines.
proposedFacts: Does the block need permanent road or gravelling inside the ADA or SRA?
Is the permanent road located along lot lines or natural boundaries where it can be?

sections.bearsOn: After a Part B harvest no site preparation or planting may be done, so the stand must regenerate naturally or the free-growing duty must be relieved.
Every Part B harvesting proposal is to be referred to the agriculture ministry.
No woodlot, community forest, TFL or other area-based tenure is to be established inside an ADA or SRA.
sections.gapNote: The rule's question lists woodlot licences, community forest agreements and TFLs; a First Nations woodland licence (created 2011) is also area-based and is not named.

sections.bearsOn: A block may deviate from Parts A-D only as limited, conditional salvage or harvest determined by the agriculture ministry and administered by Forests, or as an adjustment for Crown land adjudication.
The order reaches only Crown land and leaves untouched cutting permits, road permits, TSLs without CPs, FRPA s. 7(1)(b)/196(1) areas and that year's range schedules in effect when it took effect.
sections.gapNote: The "Crown land only" limb sits in the applicability question every rule asks.

sections.bearsOn: The order took effect on Gazette publication despite FRPA s. 16(2).
sections.gapNote: Only the Part II rule's action mentions the Gazette date; the planner does not hold the publication date. Rarely matters now.

sections.bearsOn: Sets the FRPA s. 8 period (6 months) within which forest stewardship plans had to be amended to address the new objectives.
sections.gapNote: fsp-ada-strategy asks whether the FSP states an ADA/SRA result or strategy, not whether it was amended within the period; the period ran out in 2007.

sections.bearsOn: Says where the order is filed.
The maps locate the ADAs and SRAs, but each says it is a visual representation not for legal purposes, so the legal boundary must be confirmed with the district.
sections.gapNote: The ground screen already says the maps are not for legal purposes; nothing else to encode.
